The project will include parcel acquisition and the reconstruction and improvement of Main Street, including roadway and drainage improvements to enhance the corridor’s safety, functionality, and resilience. The project will serve a predominantly Low- and Moderate-Income (LMI) community and address vulnerabilities identified following Hurricanes Helene and Milton. SUMMARY: On March 10, 2026, the Village adopted an ordinance annexing approximately 446.14 acres of land, known as Artistry Lakes. The County objected to the annexation because the annexation area does not meet the requirements of Section 171.043, Florida Statutes. On March 26, 2026, the County passed a resolution initiating the Conflict Resolution Procedures under Chapter 164. Florida Statutes. On February 10, 2026, after discussions with the County, the Village initiated the Interlocal Service Boundary Agreement (ISBA) process to negotiate the terms under which the subject property and adjacent properties will be annexed. The County adopted its responding resolution on February 26, 2026. While the Village approved the ISBA, the Palm Beach County Board of County Commissioners (BCC) denied it on August 26, 2026. On September 30th, 2026 the County Administrator and the Village Manager met per Ch. 164 Conflict Resolution Proceedings. Both the County Administrator and the Village Manager agreed to bring the ILA to their respective governing bodies. The County also agreed to bring the PBA to the BCC at the same time as the ILA. The Village Council approved the ILA on October 13, 2026.

On July 14, 2026, the City Commission authorized a tentative millage rate of 6.0543 mills for FY 2026/2027. This rate is the same as the current adopted millage rate and is 5.84% more than the rolled-back rate of 5.7200 mills. The gross taxable value of property in the City, including new construction, is $12,165,367,159. The proposed Resolution adopts the tentative ad valorem tax rate of 6.0543 mills, which is necessary to fund the FY 2026/2027 budget for the City. In November 2014, residents voted and approved funding for the General Obligation Bonds for development, design, acquisition, and construction for certain parks, recreation and leisure projects within the City. On July 14, 2026, the City Commission authorized a tentative millage rate of .2865 mills for the annual debt service for FY 2026/2027. The proposed Resolution adopts the voter approved debt service tax levy necessary to fund the FY 2026/2027 Budget to fund the debt service necessary to pay principal and interest on the General Obligation (GO) Bonds. outgoing_grants.title: Please accept this letter as my strong and enthusiastic endorsement of the Early Learning Coalition (ELC) of Broward County’s grant application to the City of Sunrise. At Broward College, we witness firsthand the life-changing impact of the School Readiness program. For many of our student-parents, access to affordable, high-quality childcare is not merely a support service, it is the deciding factor in whether they can persist, complete their degrees, and transition successfully into the workforce. By alleviating this critical financial burden, ELC Broward empowers parents with stability and peace of mind, enabling them to fully invest in their education and career advancement. The City of Sunrise’s investment in this initiative yields far-reaching benefits beyond individual families. It strengthens the local economy by supporting small childcare businesses and sustaining the educators who serve our youngest learners. At the same time, it ensures that children enter school socially and academically prepared laying the foundation for long-term success that benefits the entire community. The Tallahassee Trust for Historic Preservation (TTHP) found that the Collins House met the criteria for listing on the Local Register of Historic Places (Sec. 10-318 (d) of the LDC). The Collins House is recognized as historically significant due to its contribution to the National Register District, retaining its significant historical architectural character, and its association with Governor LeRoy Collins as his childhood home. The ARB voted unanimously to recommend that the Collins House be placed on the Local Register of Historic Places and be rezoned to include an HPO.

Following execution of the Public Transportation Grant Agreement, staff developed a Request for Proposals for an operator and, on March 22, 2022, awarded the contract to Beefree, LLC d/b/a Freebee for On-Demand Transportation Services. Service began in September 2022 with four Tesla Model X vehicles that can accommodate up to six passengers each. The program provides first- and last-mile connectivity to other forms of mass transit and offers local transportation between hotels, businesses, restaurants, residences, and shopping destinations. These services help reduce vehicle trips, alleviate local roadway congestion, and improve parking availability. Similar to rideshare platforms such as Uber and Lyft, riders within the Western Sunrise Business and Entertainment District can request a free ride using the mobile Freebee app.

The Third Amendment to the ILA was developed in collaboration between Broward County and the Broward County City Manager’s Association (BCCMA). It included reprioritization of the current distribution of Transportation Surtax funding to Municipalities among Community Shuttle, Capital Projects, and Rehabilitation and Maintenance (R&M) Projects; a creation of a new Formula-based Funding model for R&M Projects and On-Demand Transportation during County Fiscal Years 2026 to 2032, subject to availability of Transportation Surtax funding; the development of a new means of allowing Municipalities the ability to obtain Transportation Surtax funding to be used as required local match in relation to state and federal appropriations and grants; provided Municipalities with flexibility on how each will use Formula-based Funding from the Transportation Surtax; and outlined the criteria for evaluating process, documented the allocation for municipal capital projects, and included other minor changes.

Section 197.3632, Florida Statutes, requires that the City hold a public hearing and adopt a resolution of intent to use the uniform method of collection for any new non-ad valorem tax assessment program in the calendar year prior to any such collection. The resolution does not obligate the City to use the method or impose a special assessment. Staff is working to bring a piggyback contract for a fire assessment fee study with Accenture for approval at the December 8, 2026 regular meeting and the contract cannot be awarded until the City meets the requirements of Section 197.3632, Florida Statutes. To be compliant with Florida Statutes, staff has published the required legal advertisement which will run for four consecutive weeks starting on November 10, 2026. Description ATY Resolution - C26165 Proposal and Appendix Sole Source Sunbiz - Hoover Pumping Systems Corporation Background: The Bridges at Springtree Golf Club is a 67-acre, par 62 executive golf course, which first opened in 1972. Since that time it has undergone significant renovatio ns; however, the existing irrigation pump station has been in continuous operation for 25 years. It has now reach the end of its useful life as many of its critical components are outdated and beyond their typical 15-20 year lifespan. The irrigation pump station is a critical component of the golf course and as such, it is necessary to maintain it in peak condition to ensure business continuity and optimal operating condition year round to avoid any potential disruptions. The Bridges at Springtree Golf Club is extremely busy and remains in high demand among many City residents and visitors.

This portion of the project will be funded by FDEM LAP Fund, Bed Taxes through the Beach and Shoreline Program, and Regional Park Impact Fees. This change order includes additional pile removal work and revisions to the project scope resulting from unforeseen conditions and permitting reviews. During demolition, the existing piles were found to be approximately 25 feet deep rather than the 14 feet shown in the existing structural drawings, which required larger equipment to remove them. Also, revisions include changes to site and building lighting, sea turtle barriers, construction fencing, door hardware and interior finishes, colored concrete at the memorial star, and storm drainage modifications to meet permit requirements.

During submittal coordination with the pressure filter vessels manufacturer, it was realized that four (4) valved drain-down piping runs, not included in the original contract scope, should be added to facilitate rapid draining of the filter vessels down to the top of media elevation to prepare for a backwash cycle. Without addition of the drain-down piping, the filters are limited to slowly draining through the filter media, which would extend the necessary time that the system must be taken offline to prepare for backwash operation. Scope of Work The scope of work as defined in the change order includes: Per direction in requests for information (RFI) 501 and 502, furnish and install one run of four- inch and six-inch drain-down piping connecting from each pressure filter to the filter effluent-to- waste line, for a total of four (4) runs. Install one (1) six-inch electrically-actuated butterfly valve on each piping run, for a total of four (4) valves. Provide additional electrical and instrumentation/controls systems improvements to accommodate the drain-down system.
